To gain a comprehensive understanding of data science in 6 months, this course covers the fundamental concepts, tools, and techniques required to extract insights from complex data. Topics include data wrangling, machine learning, and visualization using popular tools such as Python, R, and Tableau, as well as data mining, predictive analytics, and statistical modeling. By the end of this course, learners will be able to design and implement data-driven solutions, communicate complex data insights effectively, and apply data science techniques to real-world problems.

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to machine learning and deep learning using Python, covering the fundamental concepts, techniques, and tools required to build and deploy AI models. Prerequisites include basic programming skills and familiarity with Python, as well as a basic understanding of linear algebra and calculus. The course will cover topics such as supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, and deep learning architectures, as well as the use of popular libraries and frameworks like TensorFlow and Keras. Through hands-on exercises and projects, students will develop skills in data preprocessing, model selection, and hyperparameter tuning, and will be able to design and implement machine learning solutions to real-world problems. The target duration of this course is approximately 12 weeks, with a total of 120 hours of instruction.

This course, "Nutrition and Healthy Eating: Evidence-Based Principles," is designed for learners with a basic understanding of human biology and health sciences. Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of nutrition and healthy eating principles, grounded in scientific evidence, and learn to critically evaluate the nutritional content of various foods and diets. Topics will include the role of macronutrients, micronutrients, and phytochemicals in maintaining optimal health, as well as the impact of lifestyle and environmental factors on nutritional needs and health outcomes. By the end of the course, learners will be able to apply evidence-based principles to make informed decisions about their own nutrition and health, and to communicate effectively with healthcare professionals and the public about nutrition and health-related issues.
